newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big Japan firms show modest first-half profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Big Japan firms show modest first-half profit rise.

text.p: First-half profits posted so far by big Japanese firms have shown an average increase of six percent, a corporate survey showed on Friday.
Wako Research Institute of Economics said it based its figures on interim parent current profit results of 214 companies, or 28 percent, of the 766 firms in its survey.
It said the average gain was 6.01 percent from the previous year.

All 766 firms in the survey are listed on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange and have business years ending on March 31, 1997. The list does not include banks, brokerages or insurance firms.
The after-tax parent interim profits of the 214 firms surged 20.21 percent against last year, while parent sales were up a more modest 5.86 percent, the research arm of Wako Securities Co said.
It said the results announced so far had shown that a majority of industries enjoyed larger profits, but that the oil, steel, and non-automobile transport sectors suffered profit falls.
Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses on securities investments and other non-operating activities.
